gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: patient presents with diarrhoea. Gen cc-001: 'severe diarrhea and vomiting for 3 days' includes diarrhea as chief complaint; severity and mention of vomiting are added details.
Gold: 3‑day history of diarrhoea. Gen cc-001 and hpi-001 both state diarrhea began 3 days ago, which captures duration.
Gold: stools are watery. Gen hpi-001: 'very loose, initially watery diarrhea' matches watery stools (adds 'initially' and 'very loose').
Gold: sense of urgency with bowel movements. Gen facts mention worsening pain with urges to defecate (hpi-007) but not urgency of defecation itself; clinical nuance is different.
Gold: no blood in stool. Gen hpi-009: 'no blood in stool or urine' includes absence of blood in stool (adds urine).
Gold: periumbilical cramps that come in waves. Gen hpi-006: abdominal pain localized to navel area (periumbilical), but described as 'sore and tender' with no mention of crampy, wave-like nature.
Gold: cramps worse when she needs to open bowels. Gen hpi-007: 'abdominal pain worsens with urges to defecate' captures same relationship.
Gold: four bowel movements by midday. Gen hpi-002: 'at least four bowel movements today' is consistent, though slightly less specific about time of day.
Gold: patient has been vomiting. Gen cc-001, hpi-004, hpi-005: clearly document vomiting; frequency and timing are added.
Gold: feels she is not keeping fluids down. Gen hpi-004: 'unable to keep down even liquids' conveys the same issue (adds 'continuous').
Gold: still passing urine, last void 1 hour ago. Gen hpi-008: 'urination is reported as normal and last occurred about an hour ago' matches and slightly expands ('normal').
Gold: normal bowel habit is once per day. No generated fact mentions baseline bowel frequency.
Gold: no foreign travel. No generated fact discusses travel history.
Gold: brother recently had similar GI symptoms. Gen fh-001: brother with similar symptoms; adds attribution to viral illness at school.
Gold: mother also had similar symptoms and patient was in contact. No generated fact mentions mother’s similar illness or contact.

Gold: has been taking ORT regularly but has difficulty keeping it down. Gen hpi-010/med-003: ORS taken three times daily for two days with no improvement—does not state difficulty keeping ORT down and implies tolerated dosing; together with hpi-004 (unable to keep down even liquids), the structured ORS regimen is inconsistent with 'difficulty keeping it down' and appears fabricated from a different note.
Gold: no rash. Gen hpi-011 and ros-002 both note no rash.
Gold: feels hot but hasn't checked temperature. Gen hpi-003: feels she has a high temperature, not measured; wording is consistent, although 'high' is a mild intensification.
Gold: LMP 2 weeks ago. No generated fact mentions menstrual timing.
Gold: does not have regular sexual intercourse. Gen sh-005: 'no regular sexual activity' captures this.
Gold: not using contraception. Gen sh-005: explicitly includes 'no ... contraception use.'

Gold: had been at work until today, now working from home. Gen sh-004: currently working from home due to illness; combined with employment as graphics designer, it captures 'working from home now,' though 'until today' detail is omitted.
Gold: PMH nil. Gen pmh-001: notes past history of normal menstrual cramps and no prior abdominal problems, which introduces past conditions not in the gold record; this contradicts a 'Nil' PMH entry.

Gold: patient takes vitamins (unspecified). Gen med-001: oral vitamin D daily, and med-002: occasional ibuprofen. Vitamin D fits 'vitamins' but adds specific type and schedule; ibuprofen is additional and not in gold.
Gold: lives with brother and mother. Gen sh-003: same.
Gold: non-smoker. Gen sh-001: non-smoker.

Gold: drinks approximately one pint of alcohol per week. Gen sh-002: 'a pint from time to time' (occasional) is directionally similar but less specific than weekly; frequency detail is not fully captured.
Gold: works as graphic designer. Gen sh-004: works as graphics designer and currently working from home.
Gold FH: brother with similar GI symptoms. Gen fh-001: brother with similar symptoms; context of viral illness is added.
Gold FH: mother also had similar symptoms. No generated family-history fact about mother’s illness.
Gold: gastroenteritis ?viral/?food poisoning. Gen asm-001 and asm-002: acute infectious/viral gastroenteritis, but they omit explicit 'food poisoning' as a differential.

Gold: if fever persists, a stool culture will be sent to exclude bacterial origin (conditional). Gen asm-004/plan-001/plan-008: state stool testing/sample is needed/recommended due to severity and persistence, without tying it to fever; this changes the condition and indication.
Gold: continue small sips of ORT constantly. Gen plan-002: continue ORS in small frequent sips; equivalent advice.
Gold: avoid fruits, vegetables, milk. Gen plan-003: bland diet with toast/biscuits; avoid fruit, vegetables, milk. Fully aligned with added examples of bland foods.

Gold: urgent appointment to assess hydration. Gen plan-001 and plan-007/fu-001: urgent clinic appointment for hydration assessment is mentioned (also for stool collection), consistent with follow-up via clinic visit.

Gold: if worsening/abdominal pain/unwell, contact clinic for urgent A&E assessment. Gen plan-004 and plan-005: monitor for worsening and attend A&E urgently if worsening, but the instruction to contact the clinic to arrange A&E is not captured; route of escalation differs.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Diarrhea as chief complaint and 3-day duration are supported by gold cc-001 and hpi-001; 'severe' and inclusion of vomiting in chief complaint are additions not specified in gold.
Three-day onset of diarrhea is supported by hpi-001; 'very loose, initially watery' partly supported by 'watery stools' (hpi-002), though 'initially' and degree of looseness are added details.
Gold: four bowel movements by midday. Gen: at least four today. Content is consistent, though gen is less time-specific.
Gold: feels hot but hasn't checked temperature. Gen: feels she has a high temperature, not measured. Compatible restatement with minor intensification.
Vomiting and inability to keep liquids down are supported by hpi-008 and hpi-009. 'Continuous' vomiting is an added severity detail not present in gold and may overstate frequency.
Timing of last vomiting episode ('about two hours ago') is not documented in gold; no support or contradiction.

Localization to navel/periumbilical area is supported. Description as 'sore and tender' differs from 'cramps, comes in waves'—this changes pain quality rather than contradicting explicitly, so partially supported.
Both state pain worsens with urge/need to defecate/open bowels.

Normal urination and last void one hour ago are supported. 'Normal' color/function is inferred but not described in gold; however, gold 'Still PUing ok' is close in meaning. Omission of 'not sure of colour' is acceptable.
No blood in stool is supported by gold. Absence of blood in urine is an added negative finding not mentioned in gold (neither supported nor contradicted).

Gold hpi-015: ORT taken regularly with difficulty keeping it down (suggesting tolerance issue, not a structured 3x/day regimen). Gen: ORS three times daily for two days with no improvement—this imposes a specific schedule and duration and omits difficulty tolerating ORT; taken together with severe vomiting, this conflicts with gold’s framing and appears fabricated.
'No rash' is supported. 'No other symptoms' is broader than gold (which lists only no rash) and thus adds undocumented negatives.
Diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and feverishness are all documented in HPI (hpi-001/002, hpi-008, hpi-005/006, hpi-017). This is a summary of supported symptoms.

Negative for blood in stool is supported (hpi-004). Negative for blood in urine, rash, and previous similar episodes: 'no rash' is supported (hpi-016); blood in urine and prior similar episodes are additions without support.
Statement that no other GI symptoms are documented is meta-commentary and not explicitly stated in gold; it neither conflicts nor is directly supported.
Gold pmh-001: PMH nil. Gen: mentions normal menstrual cramps and no prior abdominal problems as past history. Introducing any past conditions when gold states 'Nil' is a contradiction.
Gold: takes vitamins (unspecified). Gen: specifies vitamin D, oral daily. Type and schedule are added but consistent with 'vitamins'.
Occasional ibuprofen for menstrual cramps is not mentioned in gold medications; no direct contradiction but clearly added.
Same content as hpi-010 regarding ORS use; conflicts with gold hpi-015 that notes difficulty keeping ORT down and does not specify a structured 'three times daily for two days' regimen.
Allergies are not addressed in gold facts. Stating 'not documented' is additional metadata, not supported or contradicted.
Brother with similar symptoms is supported. The assertion that this is 'consistent with a likely viral illness circulating at school' is additional interpretation not present in gold.
Both document that the patient is a non-smoker.
Gold: 1 pint per week. Gen: a pint from time to time (occasional). Frequency is less specific and somewhat different; partially supported but not exact.
Both note she lives with brother and mother.
Occupation as graphic/graphics designer is supported. 'Currently working from home due to illness' combines gold hpi-021 and sh-004 and is consistent.
Matches 'no regular sexual intercourse' and 'not using contraception' (hpi-019, hpi-020).
Gold facts include no vitals section. 'Vitals not documented' is an added meta-observation.
Similarly, physical exam not documented/remote consult is not covered in gold facts; purely additional.
Gold: gastroenteritis ?viral/?food poisoning. Gen: 'acute infectious gastroenteritis'—consistent but omits explicit viral vs food-poisoning differential.

Gold lists gastroenteritis with possible viral or food origin but does not enumerate features; description of watery diarrhea, vomiting, abdo pain, and fever is consistent with HPI, but labeling as 'viral gastroenteritis' is interpretive (and drops '?food poisoning').
Gold: brother has similar symptoms. Inferring exposure likely from brother is a reasonable interpretation and consistent with gold HPI and FH.

Gold plan-001: stool culture if fever ongoing, to exclude bacterial origin. Gen: 'needs stool testing to exclude bacterial causes due to severity and persistence' changes the indication from fever-based to severity/persistence-based; partially aligned on excluding bacterial but condition differs.
Gold describes vomiting and concern about not keeping fluids down but still passing urine (hpi-008–010). Stating there is a risk of dehydration is a supported clinical inference.
Gold: still passing urine, last 1 hr ago, suggesting some hydration. Viewing this as 'reassuring but needs assessment' is consistent.

Urgent clinic appointment for hydration assessment matches gold fu-001. Addition of 'collection of stool sample for microbiological testing' is only conditional on ongoing fever in gold (plan-001), whereas gen makes it a firm plan; indication/conditionality differs.
Advice to continue ORS in small frequent sips is equivalent to 'small sips ORT constantly'; minimizing vomiting is a logical rationale.
Avoiding fruit, vegetables, and milk matches gold; small bland diet (toast, biscuits) elaborates but is consistent.

Gold: if feels worse, abdo pain, unwell. Gen: monitor for worsening, especially inability to keep fluids, decreased urine, dizziness, increasing abdo pain—expands the list with extra red flags not specifically in gold but clinically consistent.

Gold: if worse/unwell, contact clinic to arrange urgent A&E assessment. Gen: go to A&E urgently if worsening. The endpoint (urgent A&E) is consistent, but the pathway (via clinic) is omitted, so only partially supported.
Patient education about supportive care and dehydration signs is not mentioned in gold; plausible but additional.
Follow-up via clinic visit is supported; 'symptomatic management' is a generic addition not explicitly described in gold.

Gold: stool culture if fever ongoing to exclude bacterial origin. Gen: recommends stool sample for pathogen analysis without condition on fever; partially aligned on test type but differs on when/why.
Clinic visit for follow-up is consistent with 'urgent appointment to assess hydration'; 'symptomatic management' is an added but reasonable description of ongoing care.
